title: Completion of a monomial quotient at its coordinate origin
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $r\ge0$, and put $P=k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s\in\mathbf N^r\setminus\{0\}$ be a finite list, possibly empty, and set $J=(T^{\alpha_1},\ldots,T^{\alpha_s})$, $A=P/J$ and $\mathfrak m=(\overline T_1,\ldots,\overline T_r)\subset A$. Let $D=\bigcup_{i=1}^s(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^r)$. With maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the map sending each $T_i$ to its germ induces a canonical isomorphism
$$k[[T_1,\ldots,T_r]]/Jk[[T_1,\ldots,T_r]]\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \widehat{A_{\mathfrak m}}$$
[def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Every class on the left has a unique representative $\sum_{\beta\notin D}c_\beta T^\beta$. For every $N\ge1$, truncation to $|\beta|<N$ identifies both sides modulo the $N$th power of their coordinate maximal ideals with $P/(J+(T_1,\ldots,T_r)^N)$; these identifications commute with all truncation maps and with the displayed isomorphism. For $r=0$ the list is necessarily empty and the assertion is the identity of $k$.

source.place: Agent coefficientwise inverse-limit calculation extracted from inherited step 4, generalized to finitely generated monomial ideals; Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities) is the supporting completion reference. This statement gives the explicit monomial quotient and localization comparison, not only completion of an exact sequence.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak q=(T_1,\ldots,T_r)\subset P$ and $B_N=P/(J+\mathfrak q^N)$. From the finite monomial expansion [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $\mathfrak q^N$ is spanned by monomials of total degree at least $N$: split off $N$ variable factors in each such monomial. Similarly $J$ is spanned by monomials with exponent in $D$: each is divisible by some $T^{\alpha_i}$, and multiplication cannot leave this upper set. Thus every element of $B_N$ has unique coefficients on $\{\beta\notin D:|\beta|<N\}$. Reduction $B_M\to B_N$ for $M\ge N$ deletes coefficients of degree at least $N$. Evaluation at zero gives $A/\mathfrak m=k$, since all $\alpha_i\ne0$; hence $\mathfrak m$ is maximal.

proof.text: Write $S=k[[T_1,\ldots,T_r]]$ and $K=(T^{\alpha_1},\ldots,T^{\alpha_s})S$. By the convolution formula [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], every element of $K$ has coefficients zero outside $D$. Conversely, for $F=\sum_{\beta\in D}c_\beta T^\beta$, assign each $\beta$ to the least $i$ with $\alpha_i\le\beta$ coordinatewise, and define $G_i$ to have coefficient $c_\beta$ at $\beta-\alpha_i$ for assigned $\beta$, and zero elsewhere. Then $F=\sum_{i=1}^sT^{\alpha_i}G_i$, coefficient by coefficient; the outer sum is finite. Deleting the $D$ coefficients of any series therefore gives its representative in $Q=S/K$, and two such representatives differ by $K$ only when all their coefficients agree. This proves the required unique representative without a closure-of-ideal assertion.

proof.text: For a series supported in degrees at least $N$, assign each exponent $\beta$ to one chosen degree-$N$ vector $\gamma\le\beta$, for example by taking the first $N$ variable factors in coordinate order. There are finitely many such $\gamma$. Factoring as in step 2 expresses the series as $\sum_{|\gamma|=N}T^\gamma H_\gamma$. Thus the series with zero coefficients in degrees below $N$ are exactly $(T_1,\ldots,T_r)^NS$. The reverse inclusion follows from convolution. In $Q$ the corresponding statement is read on the unique representative of step 2, since $D$ is upward closed. In particular the kernel of constant coefficient on $Q$ is $\mathfrak n=(\overline T_1,\ldots,\overline T_r)Q$.

proof.text: Constant coefficient has quotient $k$. Every series $F=c+H$ with $c\ne0$ and $H$ of zero constant coefficient is invertible: $c^{-1}\sum_{j\ge0}(-c^{-1}H)^j$ is a defined series, since each fixed coefficient receives contributions only from $j\le|\beta|$. The finite geometric identity in each degree proves it is an inverse. It descends to an inverse in $Q$. Therefore the nonunits of $Q$ are exactly $\mathfrak n$, so $Q$ is local with coordinate maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. This uses the actual coefficient operations of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], with no assertion about convergence in an unspecified topology.

proof.text: Truncation defines $\tau_N:S\to B_N$, $F\mapsto[\sum_{|\beta|<N}c_\beta T^\beta]$. The sum is finite. It is additive and multiplicative: in degree below $N$, each coefficient of a product uses only coefficients in degrees below $N$; all other polynomial terms lie in $\mathfrak q^N$. It kills $K$. Steps 1--3 show that the induced surjection $Q\to B_N$ has kernel $\mathfrak n^N$, since it kills precisely the surviving coefficients of degree below $N$. It identifies $Q/\mathfrak n^N$ with $B_N$. The formulas commute with reduction in $N$ and preserve constants and variables.

proof.text: Put $L=A_{\mathfrak m}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mL$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The map $A\to B_N=A/\mathfrak m^N$ inverts every $s\notin\mathfrak m$: write its image as $c+h$, $c\in k^\times$, $h^N=0$, and use $c^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-c^{-1}h)^j$. Define $L\to B_N$ on $a/s$ as $[a][s]^{-1}$. The fraction equality criterion makes it well defined, since every multiplier outside $\mathfrak m$ also becomes a unit; addition and multiplication of fractions give a ring map. It kills $(\mathfrak mL)^N$ and is inverse, on $a/1$ and on inverted denominators, to $B_N\to L/(\mathfrak mL)^N$. Thus $L/(\mathfrak mL)^N\cong B_N$, compatibly for all $N$, through the original polynomial maps.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $\widehat L$ consists of compatible elements of $L/(\mathfrak mL)^N$. Compose step 5 with the inverse of step 6 at each $N$ to define $\Phi:Q\to\widehat L$. This is a ring map because operations in the completion are coordinatewise. It is injective: a surviving coefficient $c_\beta$ is read at any $N>|\beta|$. For surjectivity, rewrite a compatible family using $B_N$ and step 1; for each $\beta\notin D$ take its coefficient at $N=|\beta|+1$. Compatibility makes this coefficient the same at every larger level. Set all $D$ coefficients to zero. This series exists by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and its truncation at every $N$ is the prescribed element of $B_N$. It is a preimage. On every polynomial, $\Phi$ is its germ followed by completion, so this is the asserted canonical isomorphism.

proof.text: The images under $\Phi$ of the generators of $\mathfrak n$ are exactly the coordinate germs in $\widehat L$. Thus $\Phi(\mathfrak n^N)$ is the $N$th power of their generated ideal: apply $\Phi$ and its inverse to finite sums of products of these generators. By step 4 and the isomorphism, that ideal is the maximal ideal of $\widehat L$. Steps 5--7 identify the quotient on either side with precisely $B_N$ through truncation, and the coordinate formula for $\Phi$ makes the comparison commute with all transitions. If $r=0$, there is no nonzero vector in $\mathbf N^0$, so $s=0$, $J=0$, $D=\varnothing$, and $P=S=A=L=k$. All positive-level quotients and transition maps are identities, giving the identity of $k$. Empty or redundant generator lists in positive dimension are also allowed: the partitions above give zero or redundant summands without changing the coefficients.
